2026-10.title: October 2026 Expense & Transparency Report
narrative: October 2026 marks the launch of Ask Eve. Every architectural decision this month prioritized permanent public verifiability over recurring SaaS overhead: the site compiles to zero-runtime static HTML deployed on Cloudflare Pages, episode metadata lives in a version-controlled SQLite/D1 schema, and multi-language MP3s stream from Cloudflare R2 with zero egress fees. Because the Making of Eve bonus conversation was converted into a permanent written guide and open-source cloning walkthrough at /guide/, our audio synthesis footprint stayed well under the $150.00 monthly voice budget.

The largest share of October spending went to multilingual audio reconstruction ($112.70 estimated across Episode 1, Episode 2, Episode 3, and all 11 standalone topic splits across 8 languages: English, Russian, Spanish, Mandarin Chinese, German, Portuguese, Persian/Farsi, and French) followed by LLM inference and primary-source verification ($34.25 estimated). Every number on this report and on /ledger/ is computed at build time from the same canonical index/ledger.json file in the GitHub repository so summary cards and raw transaction rows can never drift out of sync.

What is coming next in November 2026: finalizing live crypto (ETH/Base/USDC & BTC), PayPal.me, and Stripe listener support endpoints to replace the current launch placeholders, expanding automated primary-source receipt extraction to every historical episode turn, and publishing weekly deep-dive episodes on governance, institutional incentives, and technical systems.
highlights: Launched Ask Eve across 8 languages (EN, RU, ES, ZH, DE, PT, FA, FR) with 11 standalone split episodes.
Converted 'The Making of Eve' into a permanent open-source cloning guide & full transcript at /guide/.
Published HTTP-verified primary sources & receipts with character-level transcript span highlighting.
Stood up deterministic public ledger and monthly transparency report pipeline from index/ledger.json.
